question_text:
The city of Veridia, home to several significant but deteriorating ancient ruins, faces a critical funding shortfall for their preservation. State grants, historically the primary source of maintenance funds, have been reduced by 30% due to broader fiscal constraints. The city council has proposed a plan to close this funding gap: launching an aggressive international marketing campaign to double tourist visits within three years. The council's financial projections indicate that the resultant increase in revenue from a newly instituted heritage access fee, combined with elevated spending in local hospitality businesses, will generate a sustainable annual surplus specifically earmarked for preservation. The council concludes that this plan will not only restore but exceed previous levels of funding, ensuring the ruins' structural integrity for decades.

Which of the following would it be most useful to know in order to evaluate the plan?
